correctness.rationale: For 1<=k<=p-1, binomial(p,k)^r is divisible by p^2. The identity binomial(2p,p)=2 product_{j=1}^{p-1}(1+p/j) and reciprocal pairing show binomial(2p,p) congruent 2 mod p^2. Hence H(Y) congruent 2^s Y^p mod p and H(0) congruent 2^s(2^{s(p-1)}-1) mod p^2. With valuation of 2^{p-1}-1 equal to one and p not dividing s, this constant is p but not p^2 divisible. H satisfies Eisenstein; rational affine translation preserves irreducibility. Python verifier reconstructed 189 polynomial transformations, all 4350 coefficient checks, and 945 independent point identities; finite checks only support the proof.

value.rationale: Two independently recorded all-index Apéry-polynomial irreducibility conjectures admit a substantive arithmetic partial resolution on an infinite-parameter prime-index family, with a uniform exact criterion and proof. The result explains a modular p^2 obstruction from Fermat quotients and simultaneously handles both conjectured families plus arbitrary binomial-exponent extensions. It is not merely a finite irreducibility table, minor numerical improvement, or renamed known theorem; no claim of infinitely many eligible primes is needed.
